reasoning: As of March 2026, we're 9 months into the year with 9 months remaining. Historical data shows PHEICs declared in 7 of 17 years (2009-2025), a 41% baseline rate. However, context matters: H5N5 avian flu had elevated concern in early 2025 but probability declined to <10% by April 2025. The most recent PHEIC (mpox clade I) ended September 2025. While novel pathogens can emerge unpredictably, the absence of an active PHEIC and declining H5 concern suggest lower near-term risk. The 9-month window remaining provides opportunity, but no imminent crisis is evident from the background. Adjusting from the 41% historical baseline downward due to current epidemiological context yields approximately 25-30% probability.
